stemMd: A person’s blood becomes more concentrated after water loss. Which response helps conserve water?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Decreased water permeability of collecting ducts

options.label: B
options.textMd: Complete cessation of all glomerular filtration in every healthy person

options.label: C
options.textMd: Increased excretion of a large volume of very dilute urine

options.label: D
options.textMd: Increased antidiuretic hormone release and increased water reabsorption by the kidneys

options.label: E
options.textMd: Conversion of sodium atoms into water molecules

explanationMd: Osmoregulatory signalling increases antidiuretic hormone when body fluids become too concentrated. This raises water permeability in parts of the nephron, particularly collecting ducts, so more water returns to the body and urine becomes more concentrated. The feedback opposes the original water deficit.

distractorRationale.a: This would tend to reduce water reabsorption and increase water loss.
distractorRationale.b: Normal water conservation does not require total cessation of filtration.
distractorRationale.e: Physiological regulation does not change elements this way.
distractorRationale.c: That response would worsen water loss.
